arxiv-2012-00262.creator: Ashwin Sah, Mehtaab Sawhney, Yufei Zhao
arxiv-2012-00262.description: Abstract . We prove that every n n -vertex tournament has at most n ​ ( n − 1 2 ) k n\left(\frac{n-1}{2}\right)^{k} walks of length k k . We determine the maximum density of directed k -edge paths in an n -vertex tournament. Our focus is on the case of fixed k and large n .

arxiv-2012-10168.title: An introduction to Reshetnyak’s theory of subharmonic distances
arxiv-2012-10168.creator: François Fillastre
arxiv-2012-10168.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by François Fillastre. The aim of the present text is to provide some basics around Reshetnyak’s theory of subharmonic distances, together with an overview of the main results. This text is intended to be a complement to the English translation of [ Reshetnyak, 1954 ] , [ Reshetnyak, 1959 ] , [ Reshetnyak, 1960a ] , [ Reshetnyak, 1960b ] , [ Reshetnyak, 1961b ] , [ Reshetnyak, 1961a ] , [ Reshetnyak, 1962 ] , [ Reshetnyak, 1963a ] , [ Reshetnyak, 1963b ]

arxiv-2203-10476.title: Revisiting the Design Patterns of Composite Visualizations
arxiv-2203-10476.creator: Dazhen Deng, Weiwei Cui, Xiyu Meng, Mengye Xu, Yu Liao, Haidong Zhang, Yingcai Wu
arxiv-2203-10476.description: Abstract Composite visualization is a popular design strategy that represents complex datasets by integrating multiple visualizations in a meaningful and aesthetic layout, such as juxtaposition, overlay, and nesting. With this strategy, numerous novel designs have been proposed in visualization publications to accomplish various visual analytic tasks.

arxiv-2203-17082.title: The possible assignments of the scalar K 0 ∗ ​ ( 1950 ) K_{0}^{*}(1950) and K 0 ∗ ​ ( 2130 ) K_{0}^{*}(2130) within the P 0 3 {}^{3}P_{0} model
arxiv-2203-17082.creator: Tian-Ge Li, Zhuo Gao, Guan-Ying Wang, De-Min Li, En Wang, Jingya Zhu
arxiv-2203-17082.description: Abstract We have evaluated the strong decays of the K 0 ∗ ​ ( 1950 ) K_{0}^{*}(1950) and K 0 ∗ ​ ( 2130 ) K_{0}^{*}(2130) within the P 0 3 {}^{3}P_{0} model, by employing the meson wave functions from the relativized quark model.

arxiv-2206-11562.title: A Geometric Method for Improved Uncertainty Estimation in Real-time
arxiv-2206-11562.creator: Gabriella Chouraqui, Liron Cohen, Gil Einziger, Liel Leman ∗
arxiv-2206-11562.description: Abstract Machine learning classifiers are probabilistic in nature, and thus inevitably involve uncertainty. Predicting the probability of a specific input to be correct is called uncertainty (or confidence) estimation and is crucial for risk management. Post-hoc model calibrations can improve models’ uncertainty estimations without the need for retraining, and without changing the model.

arxiv-2303-11250.title: The continuum of metastable conical states of monoaxial chiral helimagnets
arxiv-2303-11250.creator: V. Laliena, S. A. Osorio, D. Bazo, S. Bustingorry, J. Campo
arxiv-2303-11250.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by V. Laliena, S. A. Osorio, D. Bazo, S. Bustingorry, J. Campo. At low temperature and zero applied magnetic field, besides the equilibrium helical state, monoaxial chiral helimagnets have a continuum of helical states differing by the wave number of the modulation. The wave number of these states in units of the equilibrium state wave number is denoted here by p p , and accordingly the corresponding states are called the p p -states.

arxiv-2311-07942.title: A new approach to superstring
arxiv-2311-07942.creator: A. Schwarz Department of Mathematics University of California Davis, CA 95616, USA, schwarz @math.ucdavis.edu
arxiv-2311-07942.description: Abstract . We show how starting with one-string space of states in BRST formalism one can construct a large class of physical quantities containing, in particular, scattering amplitudes for bosonic string and superstring. The same techniques work for heterotic string. 1. Introduction In the paper [ 1 ] I formulated a new approach to string theory.

arxiv-2404-10666.title: Bounds on Sphere Sizes in the Sum-Rank Metric and Coordinate-Additive Metrics
arxiv-2404-10666.creator: Hugo Beeloo-Sauerbier Couvée, Thomas Jerkovits, Jessica Bariffi
arxiv-2404-10666.description: Abstract This paper provides new bounds on the size of spheres in any coordinate-additive metric with a particular focus on improving existing bounds in the sum-rank metric. We derive improved upper and lower bounds based on the entropy of a distribution related to the Boltzmann distribution, which work for any coordinate-additive metric.

arxiv-2510-21839.title: Evaluating ChatGPT’s Performance in Classifying Pneumonia from Chest X-Ray Images
arxiv-2510-21839.creator: Pragna Prahallad, Pranathi Prahallad
arxiv-2510-21839.description: Abstract In this study, we evaluate the ability of OpenAI’s gpt-4o model to classify chest X-ray images as either NORMAL or PNEUMONIA in a zero-shot setting, without any prior fine-tuning. A balanced test set of 400 images (200 from each class) was used to assess performance across four distinct prompt designs, ranging from minimal instructions to detailed, reasoning-based prompts.

pmc-10492336.title: Systematic examination of methodological inconsistency in operationalizing cognitive reserve and its impact on identifying predictors of late-life cognition
pmc-10492336.creator: Kerry A Howard, Lauren Massimo, Sarah F Griffin, Ryan J Gagnon, Lu Zhang, Lior Rennert
pmc-10492336.description: BackgroundCognitive reserve (CR) is the ability to maintain cognitive performance despite brain pathology. CR is built through lifecourse experiences (e.g., education) and is a key construct in promoting healthy aging. However, the operationalization of CR and its estimated association with late-life cognition varies.

pmc-10773585.title: Uncovering a causal connection between the Lachnoclostridium genus in fecal microbiota and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease: a two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis
pmc-10773585.creator: Wanhui Dai, Dandong Cai, Shuai Zhou, Ang Li, Jinsong Xie, Jie Zhang
pmc-10773585.description: BackgroundPrevious observational studies have indicated that an imbalance in gut microbiota may contribute to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). However, given the inevitable bias and unmeasured confounders in observational studies, the causal relationship between gut microbiota and NAFLD cannot be deduced. Therefore, we employed a two-sample Mendelian randomization (TSMR) study to assess the causality between gut microbiota and NAFLD.

pmc-11657992.title: Multiomics analyses reveal adipose-derived stem cells inhibit the inflammatory response of M1-like macrophages through secreting lactate
pmc-11657992.creator: Tetsuhiro Horie, Hiroaki Hirata, Takuya Sakamoto, Hironori Kitajima, Atsushi Fuku, Yuka Nakamura, Yumi Sunatani, Ikuhiro Tanida, Hiroshi Sunami, Yoshiyuki Tachi, Yasuhito Ishigaki, Naoki Yamamoto, Yusuke Shimizu, Toru Ichiseki, Ayumi Kaneuji, Kuniyoshi Iwabuchi, Satoshi Osawa, Norio Kawahara
pmc-11657992.description: BackgroundAdipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) are widely used in the field of regenerative medicine because of their various functions, including anti-inflammatory effects. ADSCs are considered to exert their anti-inflammatory effects by secreting anti-inflammatory cytokines and extracellular vesicles. Although recent studies have reported that metabolites have a variety of physiological activities, whether those secreted by ADSCs have anti-inflammatory properties remains unclear.

pmc-12534038.title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Routine Childhood Vaccination Coverage in Ecuador From 2019 to 2021: Comparative Analysis
pmc-12534038.creator: Jose Sanchez, Alejandro Arjuna Rodriguez Sr, Kimberlly Pamela Montenegro Cuello Sr, Abhinav Grover
pmc-12534038.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic disrupted essential health care services globally, including routine childhood immunization programs. Ecuador faced significant challenges in maintaining vaccination coverage during this period.ObjectiveThe aim of this study is to analyze the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on routine childhood vaccination coverage in Ecuador by comparing prepandemic (2019) and pandemic (2020‐2021) data.

pmc-13045933.title: Multi-Omics for Mothers and Infants (MOMI) Consortium: a global initiative to study adverse pregnancy outcomes
pmc-13045933.creator: Xin Tang, Salahuddin Ahmed, Farzana Bashir Ahmed, Vincent Albrecht, Vincenth Brennsteiner, Alan Lee Chang, Nabidul Haque Chowdhury, Saikat Deb, Matthew Gormley, Tarik Hasan, Leah Kamulaza, Javairia Khalid, Waqasuddin Khan, Rasheda Khanam, Pallavi Kshetrapal, Hanqi Luo, Tushar K Maiti, Arindam Maitra
pmc-13045933.description: BackgroundThe Multi-Omics for Mothers and Infants (MOMI) Consortium aims to define biological mechanisms associated with preterm birth, small for gestational age, preeclampsia, and stillbirth. Globally, the burden of adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) is highest in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

pmc-13144722.title: A qualitative interview study investigating patient, health professional, and developer perspectives on real-world implementation of patient-centered AI systems
pmc-13144722.creator: Natalie Benda, Pooja Desai, Zayan Reza, Victoria Winogora, Uday Suresh, Yiye Zhang, Alison Hermann, Rochelle Joly, Jyotishman Pathak, Meghan Reading Turchioe
pmc-13144722.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems in healthcare often fail to improve patient outcomes despite high development accuracy. We conducted semi-structured interviews with patients (n = 18), health professionals (n = 8), and AI developers (n = 8), using a postpartum depression risk algorithm as a use case.

pmc-13211066.title: Plant Transformation States and Exposure Architecture: A Pharmacokinetic Framework for Plant-Derived Compounds in Bone Remodeling
pmc-13211066.creator: Sara Khaleel, Tariq Al-Qirim, Ala A. Alhusban, Talal Aburjai, Thaqif El Khassawna
pmc-13211066.description: Plant-derived compounds exhibit well-documented osteogenic and anti-resorptive activities; however, their translation into consistent skeletal benefits remains limited. This review proposes a transformation-state-dependent framework in which the efficacy of plant-based interventions is interpreted through the exposure architectures they generate rather than solely through intrinsic molecular activity.

pmc-13219318.title: Fluoridation in Chile: historical context, current programs, challenges, and future directions
pmc-13219318.creator: Rodrigo Mariño, Melisa Münzenmayer, Carlos Zaror
pmc-13219318.description: As part of the Fluoride Across the World effort, this manuscript aims to examine the history, current programs, challenges, and future directions of fluoridation initiatives in Chile. This analysis describes the evolution of fluoridation practices, including early adoption, the various fluoride programs and delivery methods implemented, community engagement efforts, and the challenges of implementation.

pmc-13425243.title: Protein crowders remodel RNA electrostatics, hydration, and dynamics: a challenge to steric crowding models
pmc-13425243.creator: Anja Henning-Knechtel, Marko Brnović, Weiwei He, Serdal Kirmizialtin
pmc-13425243.description: The intracellular environment is densely populated with macromolecules, creating crowded conditions. Whether in vitro environments or synthetic crowders like polyethylene glycol (PEG) accurately capture the complexity of RNA interactions in vivo remains unclear. Using all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, we investigated the HIV-1 TAR RNA hairpin in dilute, PEG-crowded, and realistic protein-crowded solutions.

pmc-13506247.title: Coexistence of Small Duct Type and Biliary Adenofibroma–Associated Large Duct Type Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma within a Single Lesion: A Case Report
pmc-13506247.creator: Sachiko Ishikami, Sunao Uemura, Teppei Tokumaru, Shuta Tamura, Motoyasu Tabuchi, Rika Yoshimatsu, Manabu Matsumoto, Jun Iwata, Takehiro Okabayashi
pmc-13506247.description: INTRODUCTIONBiliary adenofibroma (BAF) is a rare biliary epithelial tumor with malignant potential, and it has been reported in association with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA). Although the malignant transformation of BAF has been described in sporadic case reports, the coexistence of distinct histopathological subtypes of iCCA in association with a single BAF lesion is exceedingly rare.
